subject: Post-demo recap: Dedicated capacity fit, GPU profile & concurrency next steps

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo recap: Dedicated capacity fit, GPU profile & concurrency next steps

Hi Nina / Quantum ops team —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have aligned next steps: 

- Current ask: confirm whether Dedicated capacity makes sense vs Hosted API or Private VPC, given your latency and data residency constraints.
- Primary workload profile: realtime customer chat + nightly reranking batch jobs (rough split ~70/30).
- TPS targets called out in the meeting: 120 concurrent QPS at peak (chat), with 200 TPS for short burst during promos.
- Token mix: average prompt ~90 tokens, average generation ~120 tokens (we'll validate with your sampled traces).

Immediate next steps I promised: 
1) Share a filled capacity worksheet so we can recommend GPU family (+quant) and a concurrency plan.
2) Karthik to propose an initial Dedicated pool config (GPU type + expected throughput per card).
3) Schedule a short follow-up call to review the sizing and POC scope (30 min).

Attachments: capacity worksheet (blank), a short token profile csv template, and our Dedicated options brief.

Request for you: if you can drop a 24–48h sample of request traces (anonymized) into the Drive folder linked below, we’ll run a quick token-distribution pass and update the worksheet.

Proposed times for follow-up: Mon 6/7 10am PT, Mon 6/7 1pm PT, Tue 6/8 11am PT — which works?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachments (stubs):
- 20270604_capacity_worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- token_profile_sample.csv (csv)
- redwood-dedicated-options.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Jordan — appreciated the clear notes. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we pull traces: 

1) When you say 120 concurrent QPS (chat) — is that per region or global? Our US west region is the busiest; we care most about P95 latency there.
2) For dedicated vs hosted: our security team prefers Dedicated or Private VPC due to PCI and contractual controls; however costs matter — can you include a rough delta vs Hosted in the worksheet?
3) For token mix: the 90/120 averages look right based on spot checks, but we'll export a 48h sample (anonymized) for you. Expect that in the Drive by Saturday EOD.

Mon 6/7 10am PT works for the call.

—Nina

Head of Product Operations, Quantum Retail
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Dedicated capacity fit, GPU profile & concurrency next steps

Great — thanks for confirming Nina. Quick answers inline and an ask: 

1) The 120 QPS number we used in the demo was global peak; for recommendation purposes we’ll size per-region peaks. If US-West is your primary, we’ll model 85–90 QPS on US-West and 30–35 QPS across other regions as a starting split (can adjust after we see traces).

2) I attached a high-level cost-delta page in the PDF; for the worksheet we’ll include a column that estimates per-token cost on Hosted vs Dedicated (assumes our recommended quantized runtime). This will be a ballpark until we settle on GPU flavor/packing.

3) Thanks for the 48h sample — once it's in Drive we’ll run a token-distribution pass and drop a prefilled worksheet back to you.

Karthik — tagging you to propose a conservative Dedicated config that can meet the US-West p95 target of <150ms for chat gen at 90 QPS with bursts to 200 TPS and to call out the per-GPU throughput assumptions. Also include fallback strategy (lower-cost model variant) in the options list.

Call confirmed: Mon 6/7 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Nina Kapoor <nina.kapoor@quantumretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Dedicated capacity fit, GPU profile & concurrency next steps

Thanks — quick technical note from my side before the call: 

- Based on the profile (avg prompt 90 / gen 120), an Llama2-Chat style 13B (quantized to 4-bit/fused kernels) on A100 80GB-class equivalent gives ~350–450 tokens/sec per GPU for interactive gen with efficient KV cache, depending on batch shape. That maps to ~60–80 concurrent chat QPS per GPU at our typical latency SLO if requests are uniformly small.
- If you want headroom for bursts (200 TPS), we recommend either a small Dedicated pool with burst autoscaling (mix of A100-like and H100-like nodes) or reserving additional cold GPUS for fast warm-up.
- Concurrency plan: 2x GPU pool (primary + warm standby) with autoscale to 4 GPUs for promo windows would cover the numbers above in most token distributions.
- Ops notes: ensure KV cache affinity by region; with Private VPC we can keep all request routing inside your VPC which helps with compliance but adds setup time (~3–4 weeks).

I’ll drop a short table into the worksheet estimating throughput per GPU family and a recommended starter config.

Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Next steps from our side:
- Quantum will review your prefilled worksheet and proposed GPU config on Monday.
- We'll prepare a short security checklist for Dedicated/Private to share with your security team (expect that Tuesday).

Jordan — please send calendar invite for Mon 6/7 10am PT. Karthik — thanks for the writeup, please include the per-GPU throughput table in the worksheet and a short note on expected p95 latencies for each GPU family.

Nina
